page.purpose: The diary page: the ground of every screen.

paper.purpose: Paper fields and list groups that sit on the page, separated by tone and a crisp edge, never a shadow.

field.purpose: Inputs, segmented-control tracks and other wells inside paper.

edge.purpose: The paper's crisp edge. Decorative: never the only cue for a control.

edgeStrong.purpose: Boundaries that identify a control, such as a text input (3:1).

ink.purpose: Cocoa: body text, headings, the timer and icons.

inkSoft.purpose: Secondary text and icons, tinted from cocoa, never grey.

primary.purpose: Strawberry: the primary action's fill. A soft fill, so it carries a dark label.

onPrimary.purpose: The label on a primary fill.

primaryInk.purpose: Strawberry as text or an icon: links, selected labels, the selected tab.

primarySoft.purpose: A selected chip or row, tinted from strawberry.

accent.purpose: The brand's red, used small and rarely (a badge, the sticker moment). A strong fill, so it carries a light label.

onAccent.purpose: The label on a red accent fill.

accentInk.purpose: The accent red as text: rare emphasis.

success.purpose: Leaf: goal reached, garden growth. A soft fill with a dark label.

onSuccess.purpose: The label on a leaf fill.

successInk.purpose: Leaf as text or an icon.

danger.purpose: Destructive actions only (reset, delete), kept apart from the brand red so the brand colour never means loss.

onDanger.purpose: The label on a destructive fill.

ringTrack.purpose: The timer ring's unfilled track; also chart baselines.

ringFocus.purpose: The ring during focus, and focus data marks in Stats (3:1 on the page and the track).

ringBreak.purpose: The ring during a break, and break data marks.

stickerEdge.purpose: The die-cut border around every sticker, in both themes. Stickers only, never chrome.

stickerShadow.purpose: The sticker's soft, offset shadow, tinted from the theme. Stickers are the only things that lift.

timer.purpose: The countdown only: Baloo 2 SemiBold, tabular figures, 25% of the ring's size on the Ring, 56pt on Facing Pages, fit to one line down to 0.5.

title.purpose: Tab titles drawn in the content on Stats, Settings and Notes; capped at 1.4x.

body.purpose: List rows, notes, values; system face, Dynamic Type.

body-strong.purpose: Classic's phase line, the Add pill, the editor title.

button.purpose: The primary pill's label (16pt semibold on the quiet pill).

label.purpose: Partner and next-change lines, segment labels, summaries (500 or 600).

caption.purpose: Group headers, page labels, day names and counts.

shadows.name: sticker-lift
shadows.value: stickerShadow (#4A2C2929 light, #0D070F66 dark); silhouette offset 1pt right, 2pt down; three layers at 0, 1, 2pt outward stroke, each at alpha 1 - (1 - a)^(1/3)
shadows.purpose: Stickers only: the pose stickers, today's row, the postcards. Drawn inside the sticker's SVG, never an SVG blur filter or a view shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-strong
motion.purpose: Press feedback, crossfades, entrances and flights.

motion.name: ease-in-out-strong
motion.purpose: The segmented indicator, which moves across rather than entering.

motion.name: press
motion.value: scale 0.97, 100ms in / 180ms out, ease-out-strong; Reduce Motion: opacity 0.85
motion.purpose: Every pill and button, with the selection haptic on press-in.

motion.name: phase-crossfade
motion.purpose: Ring or spine-bar colour and mascot pose on focus/break change.

motion.name: reserved-row-crossfade
motion.purpose: Presets to the cycle row on Start.

motion.name: sticker-placement
motion.value: spring 450ms, dampingRatio 0.75 (bounce ~0.25); from translateY -16, scale 1.35, rotate -10deg; opacity 120ms; 12 particles, 600ms ease-out; Reduce Motion: 200ms fade
motion.purpose: The one bounce: a completed session's sticker pressed onto today's row.

motion.name: welcome-once
motion.value: 4200ms timeline: staging, anticipation, parabolic leap, squash on landing (1650ms) with rebound, hop, dive into the mark, 10 sparkles (cap 12); Reduce Motion: 300ms fade
motion.purpose: The owner-approved exception (build 49, F5): the one-time v1.4 welcome.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: Modes, love note, note editor: the platform's own sheet motion.

layout.name: compact-height
layout.purpose: iPhone landscape: the page splits in two.

layout.name: ax-font-scale
layout.purpose: Accessibility layouts: stacked pages, wrapped segments, the stack as a list.

layout.name: ring
layout.purpose: The Ring sizes from the height its neighbours leave.

narrative.overview:
The app is the diary a student couple keeps together, the kind of kawaii stationery people carry to the library. Its pages are the screens: soft paper fields with crisp edges, set in calm, quiet chrome. Its stickers are the rewards. Pomo & Doro, two small round characters (a strawberry with one curl and a matcha dome; together they make the timer's colon), are drawn as stickers, and every completed session, landed flight, garden harvest and couple milestone is a sticker placed onto the diary. The mark, **Same Page**, is two pages of one open diary, leaning in. The paper stays calm; the stickers carry the emotion.

It is an Operate product first. A student opens it to start a focus session in seconds and to see that their partner is there. The world lends four things only: **type, palette, density, and one signature move**. Navigation, layout model and controls stay native: a tab bar, sheets, switches and pickers that a fluent iPhone or Android user already trusts. Long-distance is the lead situation, so **both partners are always in the frame**: the partner's presence, intention and local time are part of the page, not a detail behind a tap.

The tone is soft, not sugary. It is cute enough to be loved and grown-up enough that a university student is happy to open it in a lecture hall. There is one delightful moment per screen, never ten. Nothing in the visual language ever scolds.
keyCharacteristics: Paper pages, sticker rewards, calm chrome.
Pomo & Doro carry the emotion; the interface does not perform.
Both partners visible on every primary screen.
Native navigation and controls; the brand lives in type, palette, density, icons and the sticker move.
One delight per screen; nothing ever punishes.

rules.name: The Contrast Gate Rule
rules.body: Every text and background pair in every theme meets 4.5:1 for body text, and 3:1 for large text and icons. A script over the token file proves it. A theme that fails does not ship.

rules.name: The Paper Not Gradient Rule
rules.body: Fields are flat paper colours. No purple-to-blue aurora, no gradient text, no gradient buttons.

rules.name: The Exact Ground Rule
rules.body: Every screen's ground is exactly `page`: #FFF6F1 in Strawberry Milk and #221726 in Midnight Plum. The status-bar band, the Modes sheet and the note editor take the same `page`; only the love-note sheet is `paper`.

rules.name: The Theme Is The Product Rule
rules.body: Themes are part of what Plus sells, so the palette never yields to Android Dynamic Color (Material You) wallpaper colours. The one exception is opt-in: a "Match my wallpaper" theme (Android 12+), planned with the Plus themes after v1.4. Because wallpaper colours can't be checked at build time, that theme needs a runtime contrast guard that falls back to the brand roles.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Timer numerals use tabular figures in every theme and locale. A digit that changes width is a bug.

rules.name: The One Large Number Rule
rules.body: On Classic the timer is the only display-scale type: the phase line, the partner line and every control are in the system face, and no title competes. Sheet titles (Modes) are in the system face. Baloo 2 appears only as the timer, a tab's title, the welcome line and today's postcard title.

rules.name: The Locale Casing Rule
rules.body: Text is never cased by a style (`textTransform`); casing goes through the locale's own `toLocaleUpperCase`, so a Turkish i becomes İ, not I.

rules.name: The Only Stickers Lift Rule
rules.body: Chrome is flat at rest. If a control or card needs a shadow to be found, its tone or edge is wrong. Stickers lift wherever they appear: the pose stickers, today's row, the postcards.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No decorative blur or glassmorphism, including the tab bar. Blur intensity and Android `elevation` are never animated. *Known deviation, stated honestly:* the iOS tab bar is NativeTabs' system bar, which iOS 26 draws as Liquid Glass. It is the platform's own chrome, not a surface the app draws; the app tints only the selected item (`primaryInk`) and leaves the unselected items in the system's adaptive monochrome. Every surface the app draws itself stays glass-free.

dos: Do keep both partners visible on every primary screen: presence, intention and local time.
Do spend each screen's single delight on the sticker placement, and keep everything else calm.
Do use the platform's own controls (switches, pickers, segmented controls, sheets, alerts) and theme them through tint, type and shape.
Do prove the 4.5:1 and 3:1 contrast with the token script for every theme, light and dark.
Do draw every icon from the VectorCraft set at one stroke weight.
Do give every gesture-only moment a non-gesture fallback (press-and-hold "Board" for the boarding-pass tear).
Do take every size from the scales: spacing 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32, radius 8 / 14 / 22 / pill, the 1.5 pt edge, 44 pt targets.
Do keep one moving part during focus: the ring's arc or the spine's bar, nothing else.
Do keep the Modes button at the top trailing corner in every mode, so the way in is the way back.
Do keep the postcard stack's alternating tilt and Facing Pages' 1° lean; they are the only tilted chrome.
donts: Don't go babyish: no primary-colour cartoon, no oversized bubbly toddler-app UI. A university student must be happy to open this in a library.
Don't let a mascot sulk, cry, wilt or nag, and never shame a missed day or a broken streak. Plants only look sleepy.
Don't draw a tomato anywhere, or a clock, timer ring or heart in the mark: those are the category's habits (ADR-0047).
Don't fall back to generic grey productivity: a grey-and-white screen with one accent colour is not restraint here, it is a different product.
Don't overload with candy: no neon pinks, glitter or sparkles everywhere, and never more than one delight moment per screen.
Don't use purple-to-blue aurora gradients, gradient text or a decorative blur tab bar.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons. Emoji belong only in push-notification copy and in text users write.
Don't nest cards, or use a modal where a sheet or an inline moment would do.
Don't use hard offset (zero-blur) shadows or grey drop shadows.
Don't draw a sticker's shadow with an SVG blur filter or a view shadow; use the three-layer silhouette.
Don't set display type anywhere but the timer, a tab's title, the welcome line and today's postcard title.
